title: How Adam Robinson built an organic LinkedIn engine as a founder, from vulnerability to RB2B
summary: Adam explains how he built a large organic LinkedIn following as a founder, and why it works for him. He stresses authentic, vulnerable pain-point writing over AI-generated content, picking the platform where your ICP lives, ghostwriters for the early stage, and using conflict like a 6sense cease-and-desist as marketing for RB2B.

principles.text: AI makes mediocre content abundant, so authentic, vulnerable, human point-of-view content stands out more.
principles.quote: the LIE of AI is thinking that it can actually offer perspective right it's like you saw these tools and you're like oh that can do X for me and then a lot of people they're like oh I'll start using it to post on LinkedIn but it's like people don't want that crap

principles.text: Articulate real pain in detail with transparency, sharing things you'd tell a best friend, not wins and announcements.
principles.quote: I'm like in excruciating detail like articulating only the pain that a CEO of a 20 million r r SAS could experience right like in in a very clear way with a lot of transparency and a lot of vulnerability

principles.text: Content-market fit is as hard as product-market fit; expect to experiment for months before it clicks.
principles.quote: Devin Reed has this idea of content Market fit in getting content Market fit I think is as hard as product Market fit for a startup and it just takes the same amount of dedication and perseverance and curiosity

principles.text: Choose the platform by where your ICP lives; if you sell to hospitals, don't go all-in on LinkedIn, though a founder profile still helps hiring.
principles.quote: if you selling to hospitals I would not recommend going psychotic like I did in trying to be literally the best content creator on LinkedIn not worth it okay it is worth I think having a profile for other reasons

principles.text: Founder thought leadership attracts opt-in employees, because candidates arrive already knowing how you think.
principles.quote: if you can explain have a steady stream of things coming out of you that are like why you are doing things and how you think about all of the different aspects of what you're dealing with in your company

principles.text: Write for a specific audience and earn meaning-based trust rather than chasing viral reach; use LinkedIn as both distribution and trust platform.
principles.quote: the alternative is you are using LinkedIn to be your distribution and Trust platform and I am trying to like I know exactly who what I write is going to attract
